passages.text: One day Samson went to Gaza, where he saw a prostitute and went in to spend the night with her.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
He went to Gaza.
In Gaza, Samson saw a prostitute.
Samson went in to spend the night with her.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ שִׁמְשׁ֖וֹן עַזָּ֑תָה וַיַּרְא־ שָׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה זוֹנָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א אֵלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: When the Gazites heard that Samson was there, they surrounded that place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate. They were quiet throughout the night, saying, “Let us wait until dawn; then we will kill him.”
passages.sermon:
Samson was in Gaza.
The people of Gaza heard that Samson was there.
They surrounded the place where Samson was staying.
They waited for him all night at the city gate.
They stayed quiet all night.
They said, “Let us wait until morning.
Then we will kill him.”
passages.original: לַֽעַזָּתִ֣ים׀ לֵאמֹ֗ר בָּ֤א שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ הֵ֔נָּה וַיָּסֹ֛בּוּ וַיֶּאֶרְבוּ־ ל֥וֹ כָל־ הַלַּ֖יְלָה בְּשַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֑יר וַיִּתְחָרְשׁ֤וּ כָל־ הַלַּ֙יְלָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר עַד־ א֥וֹר הַבֹּ֖קֶר וַהֲרְגְנֻֽהוּ׃

passages.text: But Samson lay there only until midnight, when he got up, took hold of the doors of the city gate and both gateposts, and pulled them out, bar and all. Then he put them on his shoulders and took them to the top of the mountain overlooking Hebron.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a man of great strength.
He stayed in Gaza until midnight.
At midnight, Samson got up.
He grabbed the doors of the city gate.
He also took hold of the two gateposts.
He pulled the doors and the posts out, along with the bar.
Samson put them on his shoulders.
He carried them to the top of the mountain.
This mountain was across from Hebron.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב שִׁמְשׁוֹן֮ עַד־ חֲצִ֣י הַלַּיְלָה֒ וַיָּ֣קָם׀ בַּחֲצִ֣י הַלַּ֗יְלָה וַיֶּאֱחֹ֞ז בְּדַלְת֤וֹת שַֽׁעַר־ הָעִיר֙ וּבִשְׁתֵּ֣י הַמְּזוּז֔וֹת וַיִּסָּעֵם֙ עִֽם־ הַבְּרִ֔יחַ וַיָּ֖שֶׂם עַל־ כְּתֵפָ֑יו וַֽיַּעֲלֵם֙ אֶל־ רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י חֶבְרֽוֹן׃פ

passages.text: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
He had great strength.
Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman.
She lived in the Valley of Sorek.
Her name was Delilah.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי־ כֵ֔ן וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב אִשָּׁ֖ה בְּנַ֣חַל שֹׂרֵ֑ק וּשְׁמָ֖הּ דְּלִילָֽה׃

passages.text: The lords of the Philistines went to her and said, “Entice him and find out the source of his great strength and how we can overpower him to tie him up and subdue him. Then each one of us will give you eleven hundred shekels of silver.”
passages.sermon:
The lords of the Philistines went to Delilah.
They spoke to her.
They said, “Entice Samson.
Find out the source of his great strength.
Find out how we can overpower him.
Find out how we can tie him up and subdue him.
Each one of us will give you eleven hundred pieces of silver.”
passages.original: וַיַּעֲל֨וּ אֵלֶ֜יהָ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיֹּ֨אמְרוּ לָ֜הּ פַּתִּ֣י אוֹת֗וֹ וּרְאִי֙ בַּמֶּה֙ כֹּח֣וֹ גָד֔וֹל וּבַמֶּה֙ נ֣וּכַל ל֔וֹ וַאֲסַרְנֻ֖הוּ לְעַנֹּת֑וֹ וַאֲנַ֙חְנוּ֙ נִתַּן־ לָ֔ךְ אִ֕ישׁ אֶ֥לֶף וּמֵאָ֖ה כָּֽסֶף׃

passages.text: So Delilah said to Samson, “Please tell me the source of your great strength and how you can be tied up and subdued.”
passages.sermon:
Delilah was a woman from the Valley of Sorek.
Samson loved Delilah.
Delilah spoke to Samson.
Delilah said, "Tell me the source of your great strength."
Delilah also said, "Tell me how you can be tied up and subdued."
passages.original: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר דְּלִילָה֙ אֶל־ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן הַגִּֽידָה־ נָּ֣א לִ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה כֹּחֲךָ֣ גָד֑וֹל וּבַמֶּ֥ה תֵאָסֵ֖ר לְעַנּוֹתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Samson told her, “If they tie me up with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, I will become as weak as any other man.”
passages.sermon:
Samson was a man with great strength.
Delilah asked Samson about the source of his strength.
Samson spoke to Delilah.
He said, "If they tie me up with seven fresh bowstrings."
He said, "These bowstrings must not be dried."
He said, "Then I will become weak."
He said, "I will be like any other man."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלֶ֙יהָ֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן אִם־ יַאַסְרֻ֗נִי בְּשִׁבְעָ֛ה יְתָרִ֥ים לַחִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־ חֹרָ֑בוּ וְחָלִ֥יתִי וְהָיִ֖יתִי כְּאַחַ֥ד הָאָדָֽם׃

passages.text: So the lords of the Philistines brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she tied him up with them.
passages.sermon:
The lords of the Philistines acted.
They brought Delilah seven fresh bowstrings.
These bowstrings were not dried.
Delilah took the seven fresh bowstrings.
She tied Samson up with them.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲלוּ־ לָ֞הּ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים שִׁבְעָ֛ה יְתָרִ֥ים לַחִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־ חֹרָ֑בוּ וַתַּאַסְרֵ֖הוּ בָּהֶֽם׃

passages.text: While the men were hidden in her room, she called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But he snapped the bowstrings like a strand of yarn seared by a flame. So the source of his strength remained unknown.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a man with great strength.
Delilah was with Samson in her room.
Philistine men hid in Delilah’s room.
Delilah called out to Samson.
She said, “Samson, the Philistines are here!”
Samson snapped the bowstrings.
He broke them like a strand of yarn burned by fire.
No one discovered the source of Samson’s strength.
passages.original: וְהָאֹרֵ֗ב יֹשֵׁ֥ב לָהּ֙ בַּחֶ֔דֶר וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו פְּלִשְׁתִּ֥ים עָלֶ֖יךָ שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן וַיְנַתֵּק֙ אֶת־ הַיְתָרִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִנָּתֵ֤ק פְּתִֽיל־ הַנְּעֹ֙רֶת֙ בַּהֲרִיח֣וֹ אֵ֔שׁ וְלֹ֥א נוֹדַ֖ע כֹּחֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then Delilah said to Samson, “You have mocked me and lied to me! Now please tell me how you can be tied up.”
passages.sermon:
Delilah spoke to Samson.
Delilah said, “You have mocked me.”
Delilah said, “You have lied to me.”
Delilah said, “Now, please tell me how you can be tied up.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר דְּלִילָה֙ אֶל־ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן הִנֵּה֙ הֵתַ֣לְתָּ בִּ֔י וַתְּדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֖י כְּזָבִ֑ים עַתָּה֙ הַגִּֽידָה־ נָּ֣א לִ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה תֵּאָסֵֽר׃

passages.text: He replied, “If they tie me up with new ropes that have never been used, I will become as weak as any other man.”
passages.sermon:
Samson was a man with great strength.
Delilah asked Samson how he could be tied up.
Samson answered Delilah.
He said, "If they tie me up with new ropes, I will lose my strength."
He said, "The ropes must be new and never used for work."
He said, "Then I will become weak."
He said, "I will be like any other man."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֔יהָ אִם־ אָס֤וֹר יַאַסְר֙וּנִי֙ בַּעֲבֹתִ֣ים חֲדָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־ נַעֲשָׂ֥ה בָהֶ֖ם מְלָאכָ֑ה וְחָלִ֥יתִי וְהָיִ֖יתִי כְּאַחַ֥ד הָאָדָֽם׃

passages.text: So Delilah took new ropes, tied him up with them, and called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But while the men were hidden in her room, he snapped the ropes off his arms like they were threads.
passages.sermon:
Delilah was a woman who wanted to discover Samson’s secret strength.
She took new ropes.
She tied Samson up with the new ropes.
She called out to Samson.
She said, “Samson, the Philistines are here!”
There were men hiding in her room.
Samson snapped the ropes off his arms.
He broke them as easily as if they were threads.
passages.original: וַתִּקַּ֣ח דְּלִילָה֩ עֲבֹתִ֨ים חֲדָשִׁ֜ים וַתַּאַסְרֵ֣הוּ בָהֶ֗ם וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֤ים עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן וְהָאֹרֵ֖ב יֹשֵׁ֣ב בֶּחָ֑דֶר וַֽיְנַתְּקֵ֛ם מֵעַ֥ל זְרֹעֹתָ֖יו כַּחֽוּט׃

passages.text: Then Delilah said to Samson, “You have mocked me and lied to me all along! Tell me how you can be tied up.” He told her, “If you weave the seven braids of my head into the web of a loom and tighten it with a pin, I will become as weak as any other man. ”
passages.sermon:
Delilah spoke to Samson.
Delilah was a woman who wanted to discover the secret of Samson’s strength.
Samson was a man with great strength.
Delilah said, “You have mocked me until now.
You have lied to me.
Tell me how you can be tied up.”
Samson answered her.
He said, “If you weave the seven braids of my head into the web of a loom and tighten it with a pin, I will become weak like any other man.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר דְּלִילָ֜ה אֶל־ שִׁמְשׁ֗וֹן עַד־ הֵ֜נָּה הֵתַ֤לְתָּ בִּי֙ וַתְּדַבֵּ֤ר אֵלַי֙ כְּזָבִ֔ים הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה תֵּאָסֵ֑ר וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֔יהָ אִם־ תַּאַרְגִ֗י אֶת־ שֶׁ֛בַע מַחְלְפ֥וֹת רֹאשִׁ֖י עִם־ הַמַּסָּֽכֶת׃

passages.text: So while he slept, Delilah took the seven braids of his hair and wove them into the web. Then she tightened it with a pin and called to him, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin with the loom and the web.
passages.sermon:
Delilah was a woman who wanted to discover the secret of Samson’s strength.
Samson was a man chosen by God and set apart as a Nazirite from birth.
While Samson slept, Delilah took the seven braids of his hair.
She wove the braids into the web of a loom.
She tightened the braids with a pin.
Delilah called out to Samson.
She said, “Samson, the Philistines are here!”
Samson woke up from his sleep.
He pulled out the pin.
He pulled out the loom and the web.
passages.original: וַתִּתְקַע֙ בַּיָּתֵ֔ד וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו פְּלִשְׁתִּ֥ים עָלֶ֖יךָ שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן וַיִּיקַץ֙ מִשְּׁנָת֔וֹ וַיִּסַּ֛ע אֶת־ הַיְתַ֥ד הָאֶ֖רֶג וְאֶת־ הַמַּסָּֽכֶת׃

passages.text: “How can you say, ‘I love you,’ ” she asked, “when your heart is not with me? This is the third time you have mocked me and failed to reveal to me the source of your great strength!”
passages.sermon:
Delilah spoke to Samson.
Delilah said, “You say, ‘I love you.’”
Delilah said, “But your heart is not with me.”
Delilah said, “You have mocked me three times.”
Delilah said, “You have not told me the source of your great strength.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו אֵ֚יךְ תֹּאמַ֣ר אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ וְלִבְּךָ֖ אֵ֣ין אִתִּ֑י זֶ֣ה שָׁלֹ֤שׁ פְּעָמִים֙ הֵתַ֣לְתָּ בִּ֔י וְלֹא־ הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה כֹּחֲךָ֥ גָדֽוֹל׃

passages.text: Finally, after she had pressed him daily with her words and pleaded until he was sick to death, Samson told her all that was in his heart: “My hair has never been cut, because I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb. If I am shaved, my strength will leave me, and I will become as weak as any other man.”
passages.sermon:
Samson was a Nazirite to God from his mother’s womb.
Delilah spoke to Samson every day.
She pressed him with her words.
She pleaded with him constantly.
Samson became tired to the point of death.
Samson told Delilah everything in his heart.
He said, “No razor has ever touched my head.”
He said, “I am a Nazirite to God from birth.”
He said, “If I am shaved, my strength will leave me.”
He said, “I will become weak.”
He said, “I will be like any other man.”
passages.original: וַ֠יְהִי כִּֽי־ הֵצִ֨יקָה לּ֧וֹ בִדְבָרֶ֛יהָ כָּל־ הַיָּמִ֖ים וַתְּאַֽלֲצֵ֑הוּ וַתִּקְצַ֥ר נַפְשׁ֖וֹ לָמֽוּת׃ וַיַּגֶּד־ לָ֣הּ אֶת־ כָּל־ לִבּ֗וֹ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מוֹרָה֙ לֹֽא־ עָלָ֣ה עַל־ רֹאשִׁ֔י כִּֽי־ נְזִ֧יר אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֲנִ֖י מִבֶּ֣טֶן אִמִּ֑י אִם־ גֻּלַּ֙חְתִּי֙ וְסָ֣ר מִמֶּ֣נִּי כֹחִ֔י וְחָלִ֥יתִי וְהָיִ֖יתִי כְּכָל־ הָאָדָֽם׃

passages.text: When Delilah realized that he had revealed to her all that was in his heart, she sent this message to the lords of the Philistines: “Come up once more, for he has revealed to me all that is in his heart.” Then the lords of the Philistines came to her, bringing the money in their hands.
passages.sermon:
Delilah was a woman who wanted to discover Samson’s secret.
Samson was a man with great strength.
Delilah realized Samson had told her everything in his heart.
She sent a message to the lords of the Philistines.
She said, “Come up again. He has told me everything in his heart.”
The lords of the Philistines came to Delilah.
They brought the money with them.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֣רֶא דְלִילָ֗ה כִּֽי־ הִגִּ֣יד לָהּ֮ אֶת־ כָּל־ לִבּוֹ֒ וַתִּשְׁלַ֡ח וַתִּקְרָא֩ לְסַרְנֵ֨י פְלִשְׁתִּ֤ים לֵאמֹר֙ עֲל֣וּ הַפַּ֔עַם כִּֽי־ הִגִּ֥יד לָהּ אֶת־ כָּל־ לִבּ֑וֹ וְעָל֤וּ אֵלֶ֙יהָ֙ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיַּעֲל֥וּ הַכֶּ֖סֶף בְּיָדָֽם׃

passages.text: And having lulled him to sleep on her lap, she called a man to shave off the seven braids of his head. In this way she began to subdue him, and his strength left him.
passages.sermon:
Delilah was a woman who wanted to betray Samson.
Samson was a Nazirite who had great strength from God.
Delilah made Samson fall asleep on her lap.
She called a man to come to her.
The man shaved off the seven braids of Samson’s head.
Delilah began to subdue Samson.
Samson’s strength left him.
passages.original: וַתְּיַשְּׁנֵ֙הוּ֙ עַל־ בִּרְכֶּ֔יהָ וַתִּקְרָ֣א לָאִ֔ישׁ וַתְּגַלַּ֕ח אֶת־ שֶׁ֖בַע מַחְלְפ֣וֹת רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַתָּ֙חֶל֙ לְעַנּוֹת֔וֹ וַיָּ֥סַר כֹּח֖וֹ מֵעָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then she called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” When Samson awoke from his sleep, he thought, “I will escape as I did before and shake myself free.” But he did not know that the LORD had departed from him.
passages.sermon:
Delilah called out to Samson.
She said, “Samson, the Philistines are here!”
Samson was a man chosen by God.
He had great strength from the LORD.
Samson woke up from his sleep.
He thought, “I will escape as I did before.”
He thought, “I will shake myself free.”
Samson did not know that the LORD had left him.
The LORD was no longer with Samson.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר פְּלִשְׁתִּ֥ים עָלֶ֖יךָ שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן וַיִּקַ֣ץ מִשְּׁנָת֗וֹ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֵצֵ֞א כְּפַ֤עַם בְּפַ֙עַם֙ וְאִנָּעֵ֔ר וְהוּא֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה סָ֥ר מֵעָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then the Philistines seized him, gouged out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, where he was bound with bronze shackles and forced to grind grain in the prison.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines captured Samson.
They took hold of him.
They gouged out his eyes.
They brought Samson down to Gaza.
They bound him with bronze shackles.
They forced Samson to grind grain in the prison.
passages.original: וַיֹּאחֲז֣וּהוּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַֽיְנַקְּר֖וּ אֶת־ עֵינָ֑יו וַיּוֹרִ֨ידוּ אוֹת֜וֹ עַזָּ֗תָה וַיַּאַסְר֙וּהוּ֙ בַּֽנְחֻשְׁתַּ֔יִם וַיְהִ֥י טוֹחֵ֖ן בְּבֵ֥ית הָאֲסִירִים׃

passages.text: However, the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a man chosen by God.
The Philistines captured Samson.
They shaved Samson’s head.
After this, Samson’s hair began to grow again.
passages.original: וַיָּ֧חֶל שְׂעַר־ רֹאשׁ֛וֹ לְצַמֵּ֖חַ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר גֻּלָּֽח׃פ

passages.text: Now the lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon. They rejoiced and said, “Our god has delivered Samson our enemy into our hands.”
passages.sermon:
The lords of the Philistines gathered together.
They wanted to offer a great sacrifice.
They chose to sacrifice to their god Dagon.
They also gathered to celebrate and rejoice.
They said, “Our god has given Samson into our hands.”
They called Samson their enemy.
passages.original: וְסַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים נֶֽאֱסְפוּ֙ לִזְבֹּ֧חַ זֶֽבַח־ גָּד֛וֹל לְדָג֥וֹן אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם וּלְשִׂמְחָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ נָתַ֤ן אֱלֹהֵ֙ינוּ֙ בְּיָדֵ֔נוּ אֵ֖ת שִׁמְשׁ֥וֹן אוֹיְבֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: And when the people saw him, they praised their god, saying: “Our god has delivered into our hands our enemy who destroyed our land and multiplied our dead.”
passages.sermon:
The Philistine people saw Samson.
They praised their god Dagon.
They said, “Our god has given our enemy into our hands.
Samson destroyed our land.
Samson killed many of our people.”
passages.original: וַיִּרְא֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ הָעָ֔ם וַֽיְהַלְל֖וּ אֶת־ אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם כִּ֣י אָמְר֗וּ נָתַ֨ן אֱלֹהֵ֤ינוּ בְיָדֵ֙נוּ֙ אֶת־ א֣וֹיְבֵ֔נוּ וְאֵת֙ מַחֲרִ֣יב אַרְצֵ֔נוּ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר הִרְבָּ֖ה אֶת־ חֲלָלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: And while their hearts were merry, they said, “Call for Samson to entertain us.” So they called Samson out of the prison to entertain them. And they stationed him between the pillars.
passages.sermon:
The Philistine leaders felt happy.
They wanted to celebrate.
They said, “Call for Samson to entertain us.”
Samson was their enemy.
He was in prison.
They called Samson out of the prison.
Samson came before them.
He entertained them.
They put Samson between the pillars.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ כִּי טוֹב לִבָּ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ קִרְא֥וּ לְשִׁמְשׁ֖וֹן וִישַֽׂחֶק־ לָ֑נוּ וַיִּקְרְא֨וּ לְשִׁמְשׁ֜וֹן מִבֵּ֣ית האסירים וַיְצַחֵק֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּעֲמִ֥ידוּ אוֹת֖וֹ בֵּ֥ין הָעַמּוּדִֽים׃

passages.text: Samson said to the servant who held his hand, “Lead me where I can feel the pillars supporting the temple, so I can lean against them.”
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
The Philistines captured Samson.
They blinded him and put him in prison.
A servant held Samson’s hand.
Samson spoke to the servant.
Samson said, “Let me touch the pillars.”
He said, “Show me where the pillars are.”
He said, “These pillars hold up the temple.”
He said, “I want to lean against them.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שִׁמְשׁ֜וֹן אֶל־ הַנַּ֨עַר הַמַּחֲזִ֣יק בְּיָדוֹ֮ הַנִּ֣יחָה אוֹתִי֒ וְהֵימִשֵׁנִי אֶת־ הָֽעַמֻּדִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הַבַּ֖יִת נָכ֣וֹן עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֶשָּׁעֵ֖ן עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Now the temple was full of men and women; all the lords of the Philistines were there, and about three thousand men and women were on the roof watching Samson entertain them.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines were enemies of Israel.
The Philistines had captured Samson.
The Philistines brought Samson to their temple.
The temple was full of men and women.
All the Philistine rulers were inside the temple.
About three thousand men and women stood on the roof.
These people watched Samson entertain them.
passages.original: וְהַבַּ֗יִת מָלֵ֤א הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ וְהַנָּשִׁ֔ים וְשָׁ֕מָּה כֹּ֖ל סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וְעַל־ הַגָּ֗ג כִּשְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֔ה הָרֹאִ֖ים בִּשְׂח֥וֹק שִׁמְשֽׁוֹן׃

passages.text: Then Samson called out to the LORD: “O Lord GOD, please remember me. Strengthen me, O God, just once more, so that with one vengeful blow I may pay back the Philistines for my two eyes.”
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
The Philistines had taken out Samson’s two eyes.
Samson called out to the LORD.
He said, “O Lord GOD, please remember me.”
He said, “O God, please strengthen me just once more.”
He said, “Let me pay back the Philistines for my two eyes with one act of vengeance.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֥א שִׁמְשׁ֛וֹן אֶל־ יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יֱהֹוִ֡ה זָכְרֵ֣נִי נָא֩ וְחַזְּקֵ֨נִי נָ֜א אַ֣ךְ הַפַּ֤עַם הַזֶּה֙ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְאִנָּקְמָ֧ה נְקַם־ אַחַ֛ת מִשְּׁתֵ֥י עֵינַ֖י מִפְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

passages.text: And Samson reached out for the two central pillars supporting the temple. Bracing himself against them with his right hand on one pillar and his left hand on the other, Samson said, “Let me die with the Philistines.” Then he pushed with all his might, and the temple fell on the lords and all the people in it. So in his death he killed more than he had killed in his life.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
The Philistines captured Samson.
They brought him to their temple.
The temple was full of men and women.
All the lords of the Philistines were there.
About three thousand people stood on the roof.
They watched Samson entertain them.
Samson reached out for the two central pillars.
These pillars supported the temple.
He braced himself against the pillars.
He put his right hand on one pillar.
He put his left hand on the other pillar.
Samson said, “Let me die with the Philistines.”
He pushed with all his strength.
The temple fell on the lords.
The temple fell on all the people inside.
Samson killed more people in his death than he had killed during his life.
passages.original: וַיִּלְפֹּ֨ת שִׁמְשׁ֜וֹן אֶת־ שְׁנֵ֣י׀ עַמּוּדֵ֣י הַתָּ֗וֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הַבַּ֙יִת֙ נָכ֣וֹן עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּסָּמֵ֖ךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם אֶחָ֥ד בִּימִינ֖וֹ וְאֶחָ֥ד בִּשְׂמֹאלֽוֹ׃ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שִׁמְשׁ֗וֹן תָּמ֣וֹת נַפְשִׁי֮ עִם־ פְּלִשְׁתִּים֒ וַיֵּ֣ט בְּכֹ֔חַ וַיִּפֹּ֤ל הַבַּ֙יִת֙ עַל־ הַסְּרָנִ֔ים וְעַל־ כָּל־ הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־ בּ֑וֹ וַיִּהְי֤וּ הַמֵּתִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֵמִ֣ית בְּמוֹת֔וֹ רַבִּ֕ים מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵמִ֖ית בְּחַיָּֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Samson’s brothers and his father’s family came down, carried him back, and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of his father Manoah. And he had judged Israel twenty years.
passages.sermon:
Samson was a judge of Israel.
He judged Israel for twenty years.
Samson died.
His brothers came down to where he was.
His father’s family also came down.
They carried Samson’s body.
They brought him back to his homeland.
They buried Samson between Zorah and Eshtaol.
They placed him in the tomb of his father Manoah.
passages.original: וַיֵּרְד֨וּ אֶחָ֜יו וְכָל־ בֵּ֣ית אָבִיהוּ֮ וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ אֹתוֹ֒ וַֽיַּעֲל֣וּ׀ וַיִּקְבְּר֣וּ אוֹת֗וֹ בֵּ֤ין צָרְעָה֙ וּבֵ֣ין אֶשְׁתָּאֹ֔ל בְּקֶ֖בֶר מָנ֣וֹחַ אָבִ֑יו וְה֛וּא שָׁפַ֥ט אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃פ
